Sweden's own schemes refuse it -- eleven characters match neither the personal nor the organization shape -- and the recognizer then asks Finland for a real, permissive parse, which succeeds, so the caller is told they probably named the wrong country. This is what the four fi- fixtures in spec/fixtures/foreign/no-fi.json used to pin on shape alone and can no longer pin at all: each of those was built to fail modulus-31, so Finland's real scheme refuses them too. A recognition now requires a code the registry would genuinely accept, which is exactly why it takes a DVV-published one.

CLAUDE.md's Exception 3. No reference date at all. Finland's century is stated by the marker rather than inferred from an age, so shortFormElidesCentury is false and Format::Short is Format::Display -- which is why the short form here does not throw ReferenceDateRequired the way a Swedish short form would. It also means Finland has no observable 99-versus-100 age boundary and no observable "turns 18 today": neither is expressible through any accessor this package has for a Finnish code, so neither appears in this corpus. Both were asked for by this scheme's plan and neither can be written; see PROVENANCE.md.

Constructed, and invalid for a reason no bearer can survive: the '+' marker resolves to 1800, and 1800 is not a leap year -- divisible by 100, not by 400 -- so 29 February 1800 never occurred. The control character is correct (290200952 indexes 1), which is the point: the checksum is checked first, so a wrong one here would have made the marker unreachable and this fixture would prove nothing about '+'. Asserting impossible-date rather than not-an-identity-number is what proves the century was resolved, since an unassigned marker fails with the latter. DVV published no '+' identity and there is no other basis for a valid one, so the 1800s marker can only ever be pinned through a failure -- see PROVENANCE.md.

The same six digits and the same correct control character as the fixture above, with '-' instead of '+': 1900 rather than 1800, and 1900 is not a leap year either. Together the two pin that the date is validated after the century is resolved and not before, because the same ddmmyy is a real date under a 2000s marker and not under these two. The leap-year half of that pair cannot be written: 290200A9521 is a well-formed, valid Finnish code, and constructing a valid one is exactly what the provenance rules forbid -- 29 February in a leap year is therefore an acknowledged gap in this corpus, not an oversight. recognizedCountry is DK, measured rather than assumed: these same eleven characters are a valid Danish CPR number, because CPR's century table reads serial 9521 with year 00 as 2000 and 29 February 2000 did occur. So the value is impossible in Finland and real in Denmark on the same digits, which is the sharpest demonstration in the corpus that a century is a per-registry reading and not a property of the digits.

H is in spec/characters.json's allow table -- Finland's own control alphabet contains it -- so it reaches the scheme rather than being refused as an invalid character, which is what makes this case reachable at all. It is not a century marker under decree 690/2022. The control character is correct, because the marker is not part of the checksummed digits, so this value clears modulus-31 and fails at the century lookup: not-an-identity-number, the answer for a value that is not a Finnish code, rather than impossible-date, the answer for one that is.

DVV's published identity 010280-952L with M in place of L. The modulus-31 alphabet indexes L for 010280952, so this code cannot have been issued and has no bearer. Asked as Finnish, so the failure is Finland's own checksum-mismatch rather than the not-an-identity-number a wrongly-named country would get -- compare spec/fixtures/foreign/no-fi.json, where the same class of value is asked as Swedish.

Intermediate character C, the third of the six letters decree 690/2022 assigns to 2000s births. DVV's twenty-two published identities cover six markers; the decree assigns thirteen, and this is one of the seven with no published identity behind it. Constructed, and invalid by its date rather than its checksum: 300280952 indexes A, so the control character is correct and the century is genuinely resolved to 2080, but 30 February exists in no year. Asserting impossible-date rather than not-an-identity-number is the whole assertion -- it proves this marker is in the map, which is the only thing a fixture can prove about a marker nobody published a valid code for.
